name: desktop_overview
description: The whole Desktop at a glance: every folder's summary and what's in it (desktop-index.md). Start here.

name: list_folder
description: One Desktop folder: summary, tags and a blurb for every item inside. Path is Desktop-relative, e.g. 'Projects/MyApp'; empty = Desktop root.

name: search_desktop
description: Find files, folders and projects on the Desktop by name, blurb or tag.

name: get_description
description: The raw description.md of a Desktop folder (Desktop-relative path).

name: recent_changes
description: What changed on the Desktop recently: files and folders modified in the last N days, newest first, with their blurbs.

name: update_description
description: Improve a folder's description.md: set its summary, tags, notes, or individual item blurbs (only what you pass changes). Use after learning what something really is.

name: list_questions
description: Open questions the indexer left about unclear folders.

name: resolve_question
description: Answer one of the indexer's open questions. The answer is saved into that folder's Notes so future indexing uses it, and the question is checked off.

question.description: Any distinctive part of the question text

name: index_status
description: Backend, model, last run, schedule, problems (e.g. signed out), undescribed folders and open questions.

name: reindex_desktop
description: Update the folder descriptions now with the backend chosen in DesktopGlass. Free when nothing changed. Set wait=true to wait for it to finish.

name: get_schedule
description: When automatic re-indexing runs.

name: set_schedule
description: Change automatic re-indexing: off, hourly, every_6_hours or daily (optionally at hour 0-23). Runs are skipped for free when nothing changed.

name: set_index_backend
description: Choose what writes the descriptions: claude, codex, gemini, antigravity, cursor, copilot, opencode (agent CLIs) or apple, mlx, ollama, lmstudio, llamacpp (on-device).

name: set_preferences
description: Indexing preferences shared by every backend: blurb style, status flags, notes for the AI, and per-folder privacy (include, names_only, skip).

name: open_in_editor
description: Open a Desktop file or folder in the DesktopGlass editor (glass IDE with terminal).

name: show_overlay
description: Show the DesktopGlass overlay.

name: show_artifact
description: Display something you made in the DesktopGlass artifact viewer: an HTML/SVG/PDF/image file, a localhost dev server, or a published artifact/canvas/preview URL. Local files live-reload when you rewrite them. Call this whenever you produce a visual artifact or start a web server.

target.description: File path (absolute, ~/ or Desktop-relative) or URL

name: list_local_servers
description: Web servers currently running on this Mac (port, process, page title) — open one with show_artifact.

name: browser_tabs
description: Pages open in the artifact viewer.

name: browser_read
description: Read the page in the artifact viewer: visible text, links and form fields.

name: browser_screenshot
description: Screenshot of the page in the artifact viewer.

name: browser_click
description: Click an element in the artifact viewer by CSS selector, or by visible text with 'text=Submit'.

name: browser_type
description: Type into an input/textarea in the artifact viewer (CSS selector); submit=true submits the form.

name: browser_eval
description: Run JavaScript in the artifact viewer's page and return the result (JSON).

name: browser_navigate
description: back, forward, reload or close the page, or go to another artifact URL/file.

name: html_outline
description: Element tree of an HTML file (paths, tags, ids, classes, inline styles, text) plus its linked stylesheets. Use the paths with the other html_* tools.

name: html_set_style
description: Set CSS properties for an element. Written to the page's stylesheet (a rule for its class/id) unless to=inline or to=style_block. Empty value removes a property.

element.description: Path from html_outline (e.g. 1.0.2), #id, .class, tag or tag:N

selector.description: Rule selector (.class or #id); default: the element's first class, else its id

to.description: Default: the page's linked stylesheet if it has one, else <style>

name: html_split_style
description: Give one element its own class split off a shared one, so it can be styled without changing the others. mode=copy copies the base class's styles into the new class and swaps it in; mode=variant keeps the base class and adds the new class for overrides.

element.description: Path from html_outline (e.g. 1.0.2), #id, .class, tag or tag:N

move_inline.description: Move the element's inline styles into the new class (default True)

name: html_group_style
description: Make a new class shared by several elements: adds the class to each and writes the given properties into one rule in the stylesheet (or <style>).

items.description: Path from html_outline (e.g. 1.0.2), #id, .class, tag or tag:N

move_inline.description: Remove those properties from the elements' inline styles (default True)

name: html_set_text
description: Replace the text of an element that contains only text.

element.description: Path from html_outline (e.g. 1.0.2), #id, .class, tag or tag:N

name: html_set_html
description: Replace an element's text keeping inline formatting, e.g. 'Save 40% with annual plans'. Only inline tags (b, strong, i, em, a, span, code, br, small, sup, sub, mark…) are allowed, and only for elements that hold text and inline tags.

element.description: Path from html_outline, #id, .class, tag or tag:N

name: html_duplicate_element
description: Duplicate an element right after itself (ids are dropped from the copy).

element.description: Path from html_outline (e.g. 1.0.2), #id, .class, tag or tag:N

name: html_remove_element
description: Remove an element from an HTML file.

element.description: Path from html_outline (e.g. 1.0.2), #id, .class, tag or tag:N

name: list_games
description: Mac games in the Desktop's Games folder: title, platform (always mac), path, and when it was last played. Filter by query (title).

name: play_game
description: Start a Mac game from the Games folder. Use a title or path from list_games.
